title: Correct PTFE Tape Wrapping Direction
description: When sealing threaded pipe joints, the direction you wrap PTFE tape directly impacts whether the joint seals or leaks. Wrap the tape clockwise around the male threads while facing the open pipe end. Because standard pipe threads tighten in a clockwise direction, this alignment allows the female fitting to glide smoothly over the tape, pulling it deeper into the thread root. If wrapped counter-clockwise, the rotating edge of the fitting catches the tape boundary, unraveling and bunching it up into a lump that creates leak paths. Apply two to three taut, even wraps, leaving the very first thread bare to prevent tape fragments from entering the waterway. Have you ever encountered a leak caused by unraveled thread tape?

A plumber's gloved hand holds a roll of white PTFE thread sealant tape, wrapping it clockwise around the clean brass NPT threads while facing the open end of the pipe. The white tape is pulled taut, laying flat and flush within the precise metal thread roots. High-detail macro focus on the metallic thread geometry and smooth tape texture, shot in a well-lit workshop with soft depth of field background. Vertical 9:16 aspect ratio, central composition leaving clean visual space at top and bottom, professional lighting, photorealistic details. No text, no labels, no watermarks, no logos, no graphic overlays.
visual_story: The viewer immediately sees a high-detail close-up of brass male threads being wrapped with white thread sealant tape. The image highlights the precise direction of the wrap relative to the thread direction, showing the tape pulled smooth and tight across the brass grooves. This visually demonstrates the physical tension required and the exact alignment needed before screwing on a female fitting.

on_image_text.explanation: Tightening a fitting over counter-clockwise tape catches the edge, unraveling the seal.
on_image_text.takeaway: Wrap tape clockwise facing the pipe opening so fitting rotation pulls the tape tight.
